audit.why: Both layers read Skill, Illaoi, Illaoi, Skill, Skill, Illaoi, Illaoi, which is the packet chart exactly, and the whys agree with the sides row for row. Nothing to flip on a 49.1% win rate over 1000 games.
audit.corrected: No chart edits. whys[3] rewritten because its reasoning was impossible, not because its side was wrong.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] and mid both explain the levels 4-5 row with "your R can answer" — Zaahen has no ultimate before level 6. No cooldowns appear anywhere.
audit.why: The mirror audit caught the identical error from the other side and identified the real levels 4-5 tool: the 850-range W pull that drags her off her own tentacles. Numbers that matter: Harsh Lesson is a flat 4s, Test of Spirit 16/15/14/13/12, Tentacle Smash 10s at rank 1, Leap of Faith 120/95/70 against Grim Deliverance's 110/95/80 — so at rank 1 your ultimate cycles ten seconds faster than hers.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5 re-explained around the 850 W pull, and the 4s / 16s / 120s numbers written into the spikes, mid and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: (a) "Final Retribution" is not Zaahen's R — it is Grim Deliverance. (b) Harsh Lesson is treated as a damage ability; it is a 4-second dash that resets her auto-attack and makes every nearby tentacle swing at you, and nothing says so. (c) Test of Spirit is only ever described as something to dodge — the page never says what to do once it lands.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags the Harsh Lesson auto-reset explicitly: the wind-up is the step-back cue, and at 4s you will see it several times per trade, so recognising it is worth more here than in most matchups. On Test of Spirit, the kit says the target becomes a Vessel "if killed, or if the target gets too far from the spirit" — so after it lands, running away is what makes it worse. That is actionable and was completely absent.
audit.corrected: Grim Deliverance named, the 4s reset-and-tentacle-swing stated as the tell, and the stay-near-your-spirit rule written into breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.why: packet.defects reports three probable wrong ability names — "Her Leap of Faith", "Land Test of Spirit", "Pop Leap of Faith". All three are false positives: the names are correct and the edit distance comes entirely from the leading verb.
audit.corrected: No name changes made on that basis.

edits.after: At Level 2 Harsh Lesson is a 4s reset that slams every tentacle.

edits.after: Levels 4-5 even out because your 850-range W pull drags her clear of her tentacles.

edits.after: Levels 1-2 are even before her tentacles come online, but once Harsh Lesson (W) is up she out-trades you — a 4s dash that resets her auto and pulls every tentacle onto you.

notes: All three of the packet's flagged ability names are false positives — Leap of Faith and Test of Spirit are correct, the edit distance came from the leading verb. The genuine error was 'Final Retribution' for Zaahen's R again (Grim Deliverance), the seventh matchup in a row carrying that fabrication. Also fixed a factual impossibility the mirror caught independently: whys[3] and mid both explained the levels 4-5 row with 'your R can answer', but Zaahen has no ultimate until 6. FLAG on derived flags, not acted on: Illaoi's R carries 'grounding' and 'untargetable' flags in the kit file, but Riot's own description for Leap of Faith says only that she smashes her idol for damage and spawns a tentacle per champion hit — no grounding, no untargetability. Per the rule that the description wins over a misfiring flag, I did not write either into the page, and I would not want a later pass to pick them up from the flags alone. If grounding were real it would shut off Aureate Rush and change the matchup considerably, so it is worth a manual check.
